title: Shaheed-e-Azam
summary: Bhagat Singh was an Indian revolutionary socialist who participated in the Indian independence movement. He was executed for his involvement in the Lahore Conspiracy case. He is considered a national hero in India.

events.title: Birth of Bhagat Singh
events.description: Bhagat Singh was born in Banga village, Lyallpur district, Punjab Province (present-day Pakistan). His birthdate is debated as September 27 or 28, 1907. He was born into a Sikh family with a history of involvement in independence activities.

events.title: Joins the Hindustan Republican Association
events.description: Bhagat Singh joined the Hindustan Republican Association (HRA), later the Hindustan Socialist Republican Association (HSRA), a revolutionary organization advocating for complete independence. He met prominent revolutionaries like Chandrashekhar Azad and Sukhdev Thapar during this period.

events.title: Assassination of John Saunders
events.description: Bhagat Singh, along with Sukhdev and Shivaram Rajguru, assassinated John Saunders, a British police officer, to avenge the death of Lala Lajpat Rai who died during a protest against the Simon Commission. This act was a major turning point in their revolutionary activities.

events.title: Bombing of the Central Legislative Assembly
events.description: Bhagat Singh and Batukeshwar Dutt threw bombs into the Central Legislative Assembly while shouting slogans. Their intention was not to kill but to "make the deaf hear" and protest against oppressive legislation. They surrendered after the bombing.

events.title: Lahore Conspiracy Case Trial
events.place: Lahore Central Jail, Lahore, Punjab, British India
events.description: Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev, and Rajguru were tried for the assassination of John Saunders in what became known as the Lahore Conspiracy Case. The trial gained significant public attention and further fueled the independence movement.

events.title: Hunger Strike in Jail
events.place: Lahore Central Jail, Lahore, Punjab, British India
events.description: Bhagat Singh and other prisoners began a hunger strike in jail to protest against the discriminatory treatment of Indian prisoners compared to European prisoners. He demanded political prisoner status.

events.title: Execution of Bhagat Singh
events.place: Lahore Central Jail, Lahore, Punjab, British India
events.description: Bhagat Singh, along with Sukhdev and Rajguru, was executed by hanging in Lahore Central Jail on March 23, 1931. Their execution sparked widespread protests and further intensified the call for Indian independence.
